thread:
hana: Heads-up — tenant `acme-inc` is hitting sustained 429s on dedicated pools. Customer flagged latency spikes and a bunch of kv_cache evict warnings in the worker logs. Ticket: #4892. @eng-oncall can you pick this up?

alex: Looking at the alert. infra-bot posted a memory-pressure anomaly on pool `ded-nyc-2` ~09:12 UTC. Can you paste the evict log snippets?

hana: Paste from the pod logs: ```2026-03-17T09:11:58Z WARN kvcache eviction: tenant=acme-inc evicted=1024 keys reclaimed=3 fragmentation=0.78 region=shard-15``` and repeated every 10s for ~6 minutes. Also seeing 429s correlated to long-context requests (~65k tokens).

samuel: Fragmentation 0.78 is suspicious but not outright impossible. Is this only acme-inc or multiple tenants on the same pool?

hana: Customer says they ramped a batch job that sends multi-turn transcripts (avg 30k tokens per request) over a short window. They were on our shared-dedicated burst mode with autoscale on.

mike-customer: Confirming — we started a processing run at 09:03 that concatenates call logs. We weren't expecting such tight spikes. We saw increased errors and latency.

alex: @hana can you run `kubectl logs` to fetch the worker stacktrace when the 429s happened? Also get the kvcache stats endpoint output: `GET /metrics/kvcache?shard=shard-15`.

hana: Pasted metrics (trimmed): ```kvcache.size_bytes=2147483648 kvcache.used_bytes=2032451200 kvcache.evictions_per_min=320 kvcache.fragmentation=0.78 kvcache.longctx_active=42```

infra-bot: alert: ded-pool-nyc-2 high_eviction_rate (320/min) — triggered autoscale cooldown backoff. See runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/kvcache-evict

samuel: Autoscale cooldown backoff + constant evictions = degraded throughput. When eviction rate is that high, workers spend cycles reclaiming and reserializing kv entries causing CPU stalls and latency. Typical mitigations: reduce in-flight long-context requests, lower max_context length client-side, or temporarily increase reserved capacity.

alex: Quick repro steps for SRE: 1) Identify hot shards: `curl -s https://infra-api/shards | jq '.[] | select(.evictions>100)'` 2) Query per-tenant footprint: `GET /internal/tenants/acme-inc/kvcache` 3) If fragmentation >0.7, file a worker restart on the shard nodes to allow slab compaction.

hana: I ran the tenant footprint: ```tenant=acme-inc total_keys=76k total_kv_bytes=1.4GB avg_entry=18k longctx_sessions=38```

samuel: avg_entry 18k is big. Combined with many longctx sessions it explains pressure. Two options for immediate relief: 1) temporarily throttle acme-inc traffic (rate-limit) 2) bump pool capacity (add 2 additional worker GPUs) while we drain + restart to defragment. Which can we do faster?

hana: Support can push a soft throttle via the API key config for their key. I'll coordinate with customer for a 10–15 min throttle window.

mike-customer: OK, we can reduce the parallelism for the job now. We'll drop concurrency from 20 -> 4 immediately.

alex: I'll queue a worker restart on the 3 nodes serving shard-15 after we see the throttle take effect to reduce fragmentation. Also creating a short-lived autoscale override to allow one extra reserved slot so we avoid constant backoff.

samuel: Follow-up tasks (quick): - hana: confirm throttle applied and monitor evictions - alex: schedule node restarts and autoscale override - eng-oncall: keep an eye for fallback model activations or 503s - support: inform billing/ops if reserved capacity spike needed

hana: Throttle applied at 09:20 UTC (api_key: ak_live_****). Eviction rate dropped to ~40/min within 3 minutes. 429s decreased.

infra-bot: event: autoscale override enabled by alex for pool ded-nyc-2 (expires in 30m).

alex: Restarting workers on shard-15 now (rolling, one at a time). Logs show background slab compaction kicking in after restart.

hana: Customer reports tail latency back to normal. They'll re-run job at lower concurrency next week and we recommended batching changes.

samuel: Root cause summary for ticket: Long-context burst from tenant with large avg KV entries caused sustained KV cache evictions and high fragmentation. Eviction rate led to autoscale cooldown/backoff, degrading throughput and producing 429s. Mitigation: temporary tenant throttling, autoscale override, rolling worker restarts to reclaim fragments. Next steps: add automatic detection for longctx microbursts, warn customers, and consider eviction-priority tuning for oversized entries.

alex: I'll attach the logs & metrics dump to #4892 and mark P1 -> resolved (monitoring). :white_check_mark:
